comments.text:
You might think that's bad, but even after being sued for slowing down iPhones from the back end two months after the phone’s warranty expired, forcing people to buy new iPhones - Apple seems to be up to its old tricks ten years later. I had a perfectly good iPhone 11 Pro that didn’t look any different from every model released since, so I decided to keep the one I had. Suddenly, the phone’s sound became very quiet, making it hard to hear anyone unless I turned on the speaker. This issue appeared out of nowhere, but knowing Apple’s history of interfering with phones from the back end, I was suspicious.

One day, I was with my colleagues, and a woman I work with mentioned that she had hoped to hold onto her iPhone 11 Pro, but out of the blue, her phone became so quiet that she could hardly hear anyone talking. Then, another colleague said they experienced the same issue. Now, it seems the tactic is not to slow the phone down, but to interfere with the sound from the back end, making conversations difficult to hear and pushing people to buy a new phone. This one was so tricky and unsuspecting; if it weren't for the conversations we had at the workplace, I wouldn't have known.
